title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Competitive Methods - RFQ
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Which method is typically used to create a 'shortlist' of highly qualified vendors before issuing a detailed Request for Proposals (RFP) for a complex, large-scale project?
questions.explain: A Request for Qualifications (RFQ) is often used as a preliminary step in a multi-step process to pre-qualify vendors based strictly on their experience and capability, forming a shortlist for the subsequent RFP phase.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: For small dollar purchases that fall below the agency's formal competitive threshold, buyers frequently use an informal process known as:
questions.explain: A Request for Quotations (RFQ) is an informal, often simplified method used for small purchases where price is the primary factor, saving the time and administrative burden of a formal IFB.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A procurement professional receives three quotes for a purchase of power tools valued at $4,500, which is below the agency's formal bidding threshold. This process is best described as an informal:
questions.explain: Request for Quotations (RFQ) is an informal process designed to solicit pricing for small purchases rapidly and efficiently without the strict formatting and advertising rules of an IFB or RFP.
